newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-ROBINSON NAMED HEAD OF ARIZONA FALL LEAGUE.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-ROBINSON NAMED HEAD OF ARIZONA FALL LEAGUE.

text.p: Frank Robinson, who played in the major leagues for 21 years and was the majors first black manager, was named Director of baseball Operations for the six-team Arizona Fall League on Monday.
Robinson, a member of the Hall of Fame, played 21 seasons with the Cincinnati Reds, Baltimore Orioles, Los Angeles Dodgers, California Angels and Cleveland Indians.
In 1974, he was the first African-American to be named manager when he signed on with the Cleveland Indians.
Robinson, who is one of 11 players to win the Triple Crown, also managed the San Francisco Giants and Baltimore Orioles. He was an assistant general manager with the Orioles from 1991-94.
